text.p: Following are the highlights of main stories in Belgrade papers on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
NASA BORBA
- Bosnian Serb president Biljana Plavsic to set up her own Serb Party of BSR today, says her legal advisor Dupor.
- US envoys Richard Holbrooke and Robert Gelbard to meet Yugoslav President Slobodan Milosevic, commander in chief General Momcilo Perisic, media and opposition representatives in Belgrade today.
- Bosnian Serb Constitutional Court calls public debate on constitutionality of Plavsic decision to dissolve Parliament for August 12.
- U.N. Human Rights Rapporteur Rehn calls on Serbian authorities to immediately order objective investigation into Kosovo Albanians' abuse allegations.
- The Serbian Electric Power Industry is not for sale, it will be privatised, says Privatisation Minister Milan Beko.
- Zastava truck plant to sign 1.6 million DM credit on Monday to boost exports.
- Non-Serbs are constantly harassed, searched on the Yugoslav-Bosnian border, Belgrade NGOs say.

- Clandestine Kosovo Liberation Army assumes responsibility for August 3 and 4 attacks, in which two Serbian policemen and two ethnic Albanians were wounded, and urges armed struggle for Kosovo's liberation.
POLITIKA
- The chief economic goals - a stable dinar exchange rate and stable prices - are being achieved, says Federal Cabinet.
- Yugoslav Justice Ministry to set up a committee controlling all Serbo-Croat sale contracts to prevent raw deals.
- The latest Kosovo attacks were launched to avenge for Yu army border troops' efficient prevention of attempts to illegally cross into Albania, says Col. Dusan Vilic.
BORBA
- Serbian education trade union pledges payment of three back salaries by end August after teachers threatened not to begin school-year on September 1.
VECERNJE NOVOSTI
- Three million out of some 11 million Yugoslavs are poor, 600,000 are hungry.

- Bosnian Serb deputy PM Aleksa Buha expects the calling of Dayton II, at which the entities would become independent or Bosnia would reintegrate, which is less probable, once the international community finally realises the current process is not going well.
- Fifteen Bosnian Serb pro-Plavsic parties sign declaration on setting up a joint expert cabinet if they win enough seats at early parliamentary elections.
- Ex-Bosnian Serb leader Karadzic refused U.S. State Secretary Albright's proposal to move, says Plavsic.
MONTENEGRO
POBJEDA

- Our rival at the upcoming presidential elections will be Milosevic, via Bulatovic. We are already politically confronting President Milosevic aned his wish to rule Montenegro through his governor, says Montenegrin Prime minister Milo Djukanovic in an interview to the Vienna Standard.
- The Montenegrin Cabinet launches Montenegrin Development Bank on September 1 to encourage money and capital flow in Montenegro.
MONITOR

- Customs officers, backed by financial and regular police, set up informal ramps at Serbian-Montenegrin border to prevent circulation of fuel, cigarettes and iron. -- Belgrade newsroom +381 11 311-4254
